groups.label: General term from first term, ratio

statements.text: A sequence obtained by successively multiplying each preceding term by a constant number r is called a geometric sequence, and the constant number r is called the common ratio.
The general term of a geometric sequence with the first term a and the common ratio r is a_n = ar^{n-1}.
General term of a geometric sequence (side note). Formula: $a_n = ar^{n-1}$
Use parentheses when the common ratio is a negative number or a fraction.
The general term of a geometric sequence with first term a and common ratio r is a_n = a r^{n-1}.
When a, b, c form a geometric sequence in this order, b² = ac. Formula: $b^2 = ac$

The sum $S_n$ of a geometric sequence with first term $a$ and common ratio $r$ from the first term to the $n$-th term, when $r \neq 1$, is $S_n=\frac{a(1-r^n)}{1-r}$ (formula to use when the common ratio r is less than 1).
Equivalently, when $r \neq 1$, $S_n=\frac{a(r^n-1)}{r-1}$ (formula to use when the common ratio r is greater than 1).
